newsitem.title: FRANCE: French underwater explorer Cousteau dead at 87.
newsitem.headline: French underwater explorer Cousteau dead at 87.

text.p: Veteran French oceanographer Jacques-Yves Cousteau, who popularised underwater exploration through films broadcast worldwide, died on Wednesday aged 87, his foundation said.

A brief statement from the Equipe Cousteau foundation said: "Captain Jacques-Yves Cousteau has gone to the world of silence this Wednesday, June 25, 1997. A great tribute will be paid to him in Paris."
It said Cousteau's widow would make a statement to the media in the late morning.

In his trademark sea-blue tunic, Cousteau became a familiar figure through books and films, particularly the U.S.-sponsored television series "The Undersea World of Jacques-Yves Cousteau," first broadcast in 1965.

A member of the prestigious French Academy since 1988, regularly voted one of France's most popular men, he campaigned vigourously against marine pollution, and joined international protests against France's nuclear testing in the South Pacific in 1995.
